speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To help me understand your condition, could you tell me if the double vision and weakness fluctuate throughout the day or remain constant, and if the double vision improves when you cover one eye?

speaker: Patient
text: The double vision usually happens when I look up or down, and the weakness in my arms and legs gets worse after activity but improves if I rest. I have not noticed balance problems or numbness.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does the double vision resolve when you cover either eye individually, suggesting it is binocular rather than monocular? I would also like to know if you have experienced any recent infections, vaccinations, or if you have a history of other autoimmune conditions.

speaker: Patient
text: I have not had recent infections or fevers, and there is no family history of neurological disease. The weakness feels symmetrical in both arms and legs.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you experience any difficulty with swallowing, speaking, or breathing, particularly towards the end of the day? I will also request an Acetylcholine receptor antibody test to check for autoimmune markers. REQUEST TEST: Acetylcholine_receptor_antibody

speaker: Doctor
text: The presence of elevated Acetylcholine receptor antibodies, combined with your fluctuating weakness and binocular diplopia, is highly specific. DIAGNOSIS READY: Myasthenia Gravis
